props.title: Raw Deal
props.initialSlug: Woman's revenge plot snares cop in noir trap

sections.content: Raw Deal stands as one of film noir's most visually striking achievements. Director Anthony Mann and cinematographer John Alton created a masterclass in shadow and light, predating the iconic look of Touch of Evil (1958). The film follows escaped con Joe Sullivan in a taut revenge thriller that subverts noir conventions - instead of a single femme fatale, we get two women representing opposing moral forces. This dual female dynamic wouldn't appear again with such impact until Vertigo (1958).

sections.content: Mann and Alton's collaboration yielded some of noir's most memorable visual compositions. Their work on T-Men (1947) and He Walked by Night (1948) established a distinctive style - deep shadows, canted angles, and strategic use of light that influenced the entire genre. Raw Deal's famous fire sequence, where flames illuminate faces in expressionistic patterns, demonstrates their mastery of noir aesthetics.

The film's narration by Claire Trevor's Pat breaks from noir convention - usually male voice-overs dominated the genre, as in Double Indemnity (1944) and Detour (1945). This female perspective adds psychological depth while maintaining the hardboiled edge through Trevor's world-weary delivery. The approach influenced later noir revisions like Thieves' Highway (1949). SUBHEAD: Mann's Evolution from Noir to Western

movies.title: He Walked by Night
movies.slug: Semi-documentary style noir about LA police hunting a brilliant but deadly burglar. Features stunning Alton cinematography.

sections.content: Raw Deal marked a crucial transition in Mann's career. Its themes of moral ambiguity and psychological complexity would carry into his landmark 1950s Westerns with James Stewart, starting with Winchester '73 (1950). The noir visual style translated perfectly to Mann's Western work - The Naked Spur (1953) and The Man from Laramie (1955) share Raw Deal's dramatic use of landscape and shadow to externalize character psychology.
